title: Emrys and the Thorn
premise: Odile Delacroix, a memory-thief and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent his life erasing himself from every record—including his own. When the old gods resume answering prayers, each answered prayer burns a memory from someone in the free cities, and Odile realizes the gods are drawing on stolen memories: his guild's stockpile, sold by a usurper who bargained with them for power. To stop the drain before the usurper's armies arrive, Odile must steal back the covenant-stone that binds realms together—but doing so means restoring the memories he stole, including the family he erased to survive. In the end he reforges the covenant at the cost of his own anonymity, choosing to be remembered by the found family he once fled.
about_author: Bram Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of letters no one ever came back to claim. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things better left forgotten, and live quietly where the census takers can't find them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unpaid Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. While balancing the guild's ledgers, Odile notices entries vanishing—memories sold to an anonymous buyer whose payments arrive in answered prayers. A dying client begs him to steal back her wedding day, and her prayer is answered mid-sentence as her mind empties. The emotional beat is dread: Odile recognizes the buyer's seal as the usurper's, and realizes his own careful invisibility makes him the only one who can trace the thefts.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, joined by Sefa, a god-touched ferrywoman who remembers everyone but herself. Following the payment trail downriver, they find villages hollowed by answered prayers and learn the covenant-stone that once bound gods and mortals was shattered by the usurper—and its shards hold the stolen memories. The beat is reluctant connection: Sefa refuses to leave him, and Odile feels the first pull of a family he didn't choose.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Honest Price
chapters.summary: Odile infiltrates the usurper's vault during the army's muster, discovering the usurper isn't hoarding the memories—he's feeding them to the old gods to buy their armies, believing devotion is just another transaction. Confronted, the usurper offers Odile his erased past back in exchange for the ledger that could undo the bargain. The climax beat: Odile refuses the trade, steals the shards, and triggers the alarm as the vault seals behind him.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the broken covenant-site, with the usurper's vanguard closing on the free cities, Odile returns the stolen memories rather than keeping his own—reforging the covenant through restitution instead of power. The gods withdraw; the army, unpaid, fractures. Sefa speaks his true name aloud, the first person in twenty years to remember him. The resolution beat: justice rendered outside any law, and a thief who finally belongs to someone.
